chore(audit): add the production engineering harness

Adds production-audit/ with an executable, persistent, self-tested harness:
source inventory with hashes, a source-review coverage ledger, an atomic
task registry with a state machine, a language-aware comment-policy scanner
and cleaner, verification gates, an end-to-end environment lifecycle, git
delivery rules and reconciliation.

The harness itself is verified by 116 unit tests covering inventory, hash
drift, task identity and transitions, crash recovery, concurrent registry
writes, comment detection, safe cleanup, exception handling, maven command
execution, exit-code interpretation, e2e lifecycle and collection, gate
evaluation, git branch and staging rules, secret detection, push failure and
the completion predicate.

The harness artefacts are tracked first party assets. Only the reproducible
build and test logs stay untracked.

fix(payment): require provider confirmation before a payment is captured

PAY-01: StripeProvider created a PaymentIntent with confirmation disabled and
reported an accepted result, so PaymentServiceImpl wrote CAPTURED and
published payment.captured.v1 while no money had moved. ProviderResult now
carries an explicit outcome: CONFIRMED, REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION, REJECTED or
INDETERMINATE, and accepted() is true only for CONFIRMED. A capture reaches
CAPTURED only on a confirmed result, a provider timeout is indeterminate
rather than a definitive rejection, and an idempotency replay no longer
fabricates a provider identifier.

PAY-02: PaymentProviderFactory silently substituted the default provider for
an unknown name, and the mock provider accepts every call, so a refund could
be marked REFUNDED against the wrong provider without any money moving. An
unknown or blank provider name is now rejected, the mock provider exists only
when it is the configured provider, and the primary provider bean fails fast
when the configured provider is not registered.

Also closes PAY-08: the provider intent identifier and the client secret are
persisted through the new additive Liquibase changeset
009-provider-intent-reference, so a refund addresses the original intent
instead of searching an eventually consistent index.

Verified by mvnw -pl payment-service -am clean verify, exit 0, 223 tests, 0
failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, including the new PaymentCaptureConfirmationIT
which asserts the persisted payments row and the outbox_events rows, and the
new PaymentProviderRoutingTest which asserts the provider routing rules.

The explanatory comments of the module are removed in the same batch under the
repository no-comment policy.

refactor(common): remove explanatory comments from first-party source

Enforces the repository no-comment policy across the whole first-party tree.
4516 prohibited comments were removed from 731 files, covering Java
production code, Java tests, Liquibase changesets, application configuration,
Docker Compose files, shell scripts, load tests and the mock provider.

The removal is done with a language-aware lexer, never a regular expression
over raw source. The Java lexer is a character-level state machine that
distinguishes code, line comments, block comments, string literals, text
blocks and character literals, and that honours escape sequences and Java
unicode escapes, so a double slash inside a string, a block comment marker
inside a text block and embedded SQL are never treated as a comment. The
shell lexer resolves quoting and heredoc bodies, so a parameter expansion and
a JavaScript regular expression are never mangled. The YAML lexer only treats
a hash as a comment where the syntax allows one.

Mandatory copyright and licence notices, generated-file markers, compiler,
formatter and linter directives, source-map directives and interpreter
shebangs are preserved and documented in
production-audit/config/comment-policy.json. The removed rationale is
archived verbatim in production-audit/architecture/comment-rationale.md, so no
design intent is lost.

Verification: harness verify --suite comments --deep reports zero prohibited
comments across 1141 files and proves that 1031 changed files are byte
identical to the baseline revision once the same comments are removed, which
demonstrates that no executable code changed. The full reactor build
./mvnw -B -ntp clean verify succeeds with exit 0 and 1931 tests, 0 failures,
0 errors, 0 skipped, including the integration tests that run against real
PostgreSQL 16 and Kafka containers.

Also removes src/main/java/org/example/Main.java, an IntelliJ scaffold that
is not part of any Maven module and calls a Kotlin-only helper.

fix(harness): make the secret scanner path aware and free of false positives

The commit gate flagged the harness own synthetic fixtures and several
legitimate source constructs as secrets. The scanner now separates the two
classes of finding. A credential shaped token, such as a provider key, an
access key, a webhook signing secret, a private key block or a database url
with an inline password, is flagged in any file. A key equals value
assignment is flagged only in a non test source and only when the value is a
literal rather than a variable reference, a placeholder or a test mode
credential.

The allow list of synthetic fixtures is now a documented file, and the staged
content is scanned per file so a finding is attributable to a path.

The harness self verification suite still passes with 116 tests.

fix(gateway): derive the rate-limit identity from the transport peer

GW-01: the client address was taken by indexing into the caller supplied
X-Forwarded-For header with a hop count, and no trusted proxy allowlist
existed anywhere in the repository, so a client chose its own rate limit
bucket and its own admin allowlist verdict. The client address is now the
transport peer address. A forwarding header is consulted only through the
explicit gateway.trusted-proxy.cidrs allowlist, and when that allowlist is
absent no forwarding header is trusted at all. The gateway refuses to start
when the framework is configured to rewrite the remote address from a header.

GW-02: a non literal forwarding entry was turned into a socket address, which
performed a name resolution on the reactor event loop, and the resolved name
became the Redis key, so every request received a fresh full budget and a new
Redis key. A value that enters a rate limit key is now parsed as a literal
address by a dedicated parser that accepts IPv4 and IPv6 only. A value that is
not a literal address is discarded and the peer address is used instead. No
request supplied value triggers a name resolution any more.

GW-03: the two framework limiters failed open on a Redis outage while the edge
limiter failed closed, and the source comment asserted the opposite of the
code. All layers now share one policy, gateway.rate-limit.outage-policy,
which defaults to fail closed.

GW-05: the edge bucket computed its refill from the gateway JVM clock while the
framework buckets used the Redis clock, so a clock skew between replicas
drifted the shared budget. The refill is now computed inside the Redis script
from the Redis server clock.

GW-07: the layers disagreed on the rejection contract, one returned an empty
body, another a fleet envelope, one set the remaining header twice and the
sentinel value minus one leaked to clients. Every rejection now returns the
same status, the same envelope and the same headers, including Retry-After.

The outage guard takes a supplier for the continuation, so the route chain is
no longer invoked when the gateway rejects a request.

SEC-01: the platform user was resolved in the wrong key space. The entity
carries a generated surrogate primary key and a separate unique identity
provider identifier, but the self service profile and address surfaces looked
the row up by the surrogate using the token subject, so they could never
resolve a row. The subject is now resolved through the external identifier
lookup and every call site uses it.

SL-24: the authorization guard returned without objection when the security
context was empty, so an unauthenticated caller passed a guard that is meant
to authorize. It now raises on an empty context, an unauthenticated principal
and a missing principal. The inventory controller test was updated to install
an authenticated order service principal, because it had encoded the previous
fail open behaviour.

The token authorised party claim is now extracted from the shared library so a
service role caller can be bound to the user it acts for.

Verified by ./mvnw -B -ntp clean verify, exit 0. The gateway module runs 177
tests and the auth, common-security, inventory, payment, promotion and tax
modules all pass. The comment compliance gate reports zero prohibited comments
across 1138 files.

fix(order,inventory,kafka,search,promotion): close the distributed correctness defects

OI-01: the inventory reserve was not idempotent. The stock decrement and the
reservation insert ran unconditionally, so a duplicate request decremented the
stock twice and created a second hold. The reserve now claims an idempotency
key at the database level with the unique constraint uk_reservations_idempotency_key,
and the reservation row is inserted and flushed before the decrement, so a
duplicate can never touch the stock. The same key with a different product or
quantity is a conflict, and a request without a key keeps the previous
behaviour. The key travels as an optional Idempotency-Key header so no request
shape changed. The reserve response also carried a null reservation id because
the managed copy was discarded by the version check, which left the order side
holding a null reservation that its compensation could not release; the reserve
now uses the entity returned by the save.

OI-02: a failed stock release in the confirmation compensation was swallowed,
so the stock stayed reserved forever. The failure is now recorded in the
existing failed_compensations ledger with the new reservation and promotion
kinds, and a sweeper claims the due entries with one conditional update, so
exactly one replica dispatches each entry, and the attempt count is bounded.

SEC-02: the delegated order read returned the delivered order items of any
user to any service-role client. The endpoint now answers the eligibility
question it actually exists for and returns the determination and the count,
so no cross-user order data leaves the service, and the caller is checked
against the platform service allow list. The rating service reads the new
contract and no longer receives another user's order lines.

SL-08, SL-35, SL-34, SL-05, SL-36: the consumer wire mapper is now a Jackson 3
mapper that tolerates an additive event field while a malformed record is still
rejected into the dead-letter path, every listener factory has a dead-letter
recoverer so an exhausted record is published rather than skipped, the replay
endpoint requires an administrative role and validates the topic against the
topic contract, the replay keeps its offsets so a record is published once in
total, and the shared consumer configuration pins the commit semantics instead
of inheriting a framework default.

CAT-01: the search projection applied every product event unconditionally, so an
event describing an older state rolled the document back. The event already
carries the producer timestamp, and the index now writes with the external
version semantics, so a stale event is rejected and a redelivered event is a
no-op. The conflict is handled on the exception type the configured transport
actually raises, which was an unreachable branch before, so a stale event is
ignored instead of failing the index write.

CAT-07: the promotion quota was enforced by a read-then-write count, so two
concurrent redemptions of the last coupon both won. The quota is now claimed by
an atomic conditional statement per user and per campaign, the counters are
released when the reservation is released, and the schema change is additive.

The authorization guard is now declared by its own auto-configuration, so the
bean exists whenever the platform security classes are on the classpath and not
only when the web security posture is enabled.

Verified by ./mvnw -B -ntp clean verify, exit 0, 2030 tests, 0 failures, 0
errors, 0 skipped. The comment compliance gate reports zero prohibited
comments across 1136 files and proves 1074 changed files byte identical to the
baseline once the same comments are removed.

chore(e2e): make the end-to-end environment reproducible and the payment contract explicit

The compose stack could not start two of its services and the payment flow
could not be exercised end to end, so the environment is fixed and the
correction is recorded.

shipping-service declared spring-boot-restclient with test scope, which
overrode the compile scoped dependency the shared library provides, so the
RestClient.Builder auto configuration was absent at runtime and the service
could not start at all. The same wrong scope in payment-service and
rating-service is removed. The compose stack also never supplied the GHTK
webhook secret that the shipping configuration requires, so the container
could not start as shipped. Both the secret and the new proxy and outage
settings are now declared in the compose file and documented in the
environment templates.

The Stripe provider endpoint is configurable, so the end-to-end run can use the
official Stripe test server instead of a real account. No real payment is ever
created and no real credential is ever used.

The rate-limit outage policy, the trusted proxy allow list and the Stripe
endpoint are configuration, so they are declared in the compose file and in
both environment templates, and the gateway refuses to start when the
forwarding header strategy would let the framework rewrite the client address.

The payment collection encoded the contract that a capture immediately marks a
payment captured, which was the defect the provider confirmation work removed.
A Stripe intent that was created without confirmation is confirmed by the
client, and the provider then notifies the platform, so the collection now
asserts that a capture leaves the payment pending with a client secret, adds
a scenario that delivers a signed provider webhook, and then asserts that the
payment is captured. The webhook is signed with the Stripe scheme in the
collection script, so the signature verification path is exercised rather than
bypassed.

The end-to-end run of the business flow collection is now 42 assertions with 1
remaining failure.
